questions.q: What is Application Insights, as this lesson describes it?
options: Azure Monitor's application-performance-monitoring feature, focused on one running application's requests, dependencies, and exceptions
A standalone product unrelated to Azure Monitor
A replacement for the Log Analytics workspace that uses a different query language
A tool that only works for applications hosted outside of Azure
questions.explain: Application Insights is Azure Monitor's APM lens aimed at a single application, and it writes into the same kind of Log Analytics-backed tables, queried with the same KQL.

questions.q: What is the difference between SDK-based instrumentation and codeless monitoring in Application Insights?
options: Codeless monitoring is only available for on-premises applications
SDK-based instrumentation cannot capture exceptions, only requests
SDK-based instrumentation adds a package and connection string to application code for the richest detail; codeless monitoring is an agent that captures core signals without touching the source code
There is no real difference between the two options
questions.explain: SDK-based instrumentation gives the richest, most customizable telemetry at the cost of touching the code; codeless monitoring captures the same core signals via a platform-level agent instead.

questions.q: What does the `dependencies` table in Application Insights record?
options: Every outbound call the application made — a database query, an HTTP call, a cache lookup — with its own duration and success flag
Only unhandled exceptions and their stack traces
Only the names of Azure resources in the subscription
The Activity Log's control-plane operations
questions.explain: dependencies captures every outbound call an application makes, each with its own duration and success status, distinct from the inbound requests table.

questions.q: What field links every telemetry row from a single logical request across the requests, dependencies, and exceptions tables?
options: `Caller`
`CounterValue`
`ActivityStatusValue`
`operation_Id`
questions.explain: operation_Id is shared by every row Application Insights writes for one logical request, which is what lets you reconstruct the full call chain for a single slow or failed request.

questions.q: What does the Application Map feature show, without requiring a KQL query?
options: A list of every diagnostic setting configured in the subscription
A diagram of every component the application talks to, with failure rates and durations annotated on each connection
A raw export of the AzureActivity table
A list of all Log Analytics workspaces in the tenant
questions.explain: The Application Map visualizes the application's dependencies as a diagram with failure rate and duration annotations, letting you spot a dragging downstream service visually.
